decision_note: Primary Erysimum capitatum programme combines pollinator and herbivore observations/experiments across four populations and two years, including floral traits, fitness and context-dependent selection; retain for multi-agent geographic-mosaic adjudication.
Cytinus study focuses floral signals establishing ant pollination mutualism; the ants are pollinators and no focal plant antagonist/exploiter response is measured.
Gorteria study tests pollinator phylogeography and mate preference as drivers of floral divergence without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.
Bat-flower network study tests spatiotemporal overlap and morphology in plant-pollinator interactions without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Science special-issue introduction on plant volatiles is a brief editorial overview rather than an independent primary study or substantive focused SCH synthesis.

Sidalcea hendersonii thesis underlies a gynodioecy programme with bumblebee pollination and specialist pre-dispersal weevil seed predation; retain for sex-biased pollination/seed-predation adjudication.
Clarkia/Petunia study resolves phenylpropene synthase lineages and enzyme specificity; pollinator attraction and defence are motivating functions rather than measured receiver responses.
Nicotiana africana experiment measures herbivory and alkaloid responses but infers that pollinators should be unaffected from nectar chemistry rather than measuring pollinator response/service.
Highbush-blueberry dissertation focuses crop pollination ecology and beneficial pollinators without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel in the source description.
Acacia greggii dissertation concerns dispersal and gene flow rather than a focal pollinator-antagonist floral-trait system.

Focused review explicitly synthesizes plant-mediated links from herbivory through floral traits and pollinator attraction to fruit/seed production; retain as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material.
Ascosphaera contamination experiment measures pollinator avoidance of flowers, but the fungus is a bee parasite rather than a plant antagonist/exploiter acting on plant fitness.
Genomics perspective on plant-pollinator interactions is broad and pollinator-focused rather than an independent study or focused pollinator-antagonist floral-trait synthesis.

Primary 1884-species comparative analysis links insect-herbivore richness to floral sexual/mating traits and pollinator dependence; retain for macroevolutionary antagonist-reproductive-strategy adjudication.
Repository identity of the 2026 Red Queen floral mating-strategy study; retain at title/abstract stage and resolve report dependence with SCHPRISMA-000810 at full text.
American Journal of Botany commentary advocates comparative biochemistry broadly and is not an independent primary study or focused SCH synthesis.
Mediterranean floral-evolution review is centered on pollinator-mediated evolution; antagonistic forces are contextual rather than a focal shared-trait synthesis.

Repository identity of the Veratrum mast-flowering programme measuring pollination success and herbivore/seed-predator damage across populations and years; retain and resolve report dependence at full text.

Primary Veratrum study jointly measures fruit-set success and herbivorous/seed-predator damage across 12 populations and multiple years; retain for density-dependent pollination-versus-predator-satiation adjudication.
Focused nectar-robbing review integrates legitimate visitation, robbing behaviour, plant fitness and floral evolution; retain as relevant pollinator-exploiter synthesis/source-chasing material.
Cape-fynbos thesis experimentally adds managed honeybee hives and measures competing flower-visitor guilds but does not establish a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.

Primary Breynia floral-scent study concerns an obligate pollination-seed-consumption mutualism and post-pollination scent change that may limit Epicephala overexploitation; retain for coupled pollinator-seed-predator signal adjudication.
Sunbird visitation and pollen-transport network study concerns pollination structure without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
New Phytologist commentary on carrion-flower scent is a short commentary on pollination chemistry rather than an independent primary study or focused SCH synthesis.
Conference-slide record links Schiedea volatile-emission timing to a crepuscular pollinator but contains no focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.
